root.label: Brookings analysis of USPS size, workforce, locations, and revenue

events.label: Brookings analysis of USPS size, workforce, locations, and revenue

slots.name: delivery frequency
slots.sentence: USPS is bound by law to a duty that no private company shares: a Universal Service Obligation (USO) that requires it to deliver to every address, six days per week, at uniform and affordable prices.

slots.name: USPS workforce
slots.sentence: With about 600,000 workers, USPS is the third-largest employer in the United States, behind only Walmart and Amazon (Figure 1).

slots.name: Black worker share
slots.sentence: Nearly 30% of postal workers are Black, more than double their share of the national labor force .

slots.name: Defense civilian workforce
slots.sentence: Only the Department of Defense employs more people, and the Postal Service workforce comes close to the size of Defense’s entire civilian arm (about 685,000 ).

slots.name: pension beneficiaries
slots.sentence: Alongside the workers on its rolls today, more than 700,000 retirees and survivors draw a USPS pension.

slots.name: income-dependent people
slots.sentence: Since 2007, it has posted net losses nearly every year as letter mail, its core revenue source , has fallen by half .

slots.name: post office count
slots.sentence: Its network of roughly 33,700 post offices outnumbers every private chain, with thousands more locations than Subway or Dollar General, the largest by store count, and more than twice as many as McDonald’s (Figure 2).

slots.name: USPS revenue
slots.sentence: In fiscal year 2025, it took in $81.4 billion in revenue, on par with FedEx ( $87.9 billion ) and UPS ( $88.7 billion ).

slots.name: package volume
slots.sentence: UPS alone hands USPS nearly a million packages a day to finish the last mile, deliveries it cannot make as cheaply itself.

slots.name: borrowing limit status
slots.sentence: It has now hit its statutory borrowing limit, and its leadership ha s warned that it could be out of cash within the year, save for extraordinary measures.
